scope: Experimental single-domain geometric-nonlinear static analysis with finite-deformation kinematics, isotropic linear-elastic material, ordered proportional load steps, automatic increments, explicit iteration/cutback controls, and normalized force-displacement history.

lanes.acceptance: A distinct nonlinear_static union member and provider profile require finite-deformation/finite-strain quasi-static elastic assumptions, one domain, fixed supports, supported loads, no interactions, ordered unique steps, complete load ownership, bounded 0..1 amplitudes, and explicit increment/iteration/cutback controls before geometry transfer. The current CalculiX profile explicitly admits only one shared amplitude shape per step.

The CalculiX adapter deterministically emits one NLGEOM static step per requested step, STEP TIME piecewise-linear amplitudes, OP=NEW load state, bounded automatic increments, maximum iterations, maximum cutbacks, divergence cutback factor, and increment-frequency response output.

Bounded status and response parsers require every requested step to finish, reject unordered or incomplete records, cross-check one complete response frame per converged increment, interpolate declared load scales, and publish final nonlinear field identity.

A real elastic cantilever records two ordered load ramps, finite support-force balance, monotonic displacement growth, and a measurable separation from the small-displacement reference at the same final dead load.

Three meshes demonstrate contracting final-displacement change, while three maximum-increment ceilings demonstrate contracting force-displacement curve change at common 25/50/75/100 percent load samples.
Deliberate increment exhaustion and active cancellation fail closed, quarantine partial histories and fields, terminate descendants, remove native files, and resist late-result resurrection.
An independent qualified engineer approves the finite-deformation formulation, load-path semantics, fixtures, tolerances, parser evidence, limitations, and exact reviewed commit.
